The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Glam Behavior (1968-1969)
podcast.body: As early as 1968 and 1969, Joe Brieaz exhibited behavior that was "absolutely glam," predating the mainstream glam movement by three or four years. His first work with his band Pigeon in 1969 already contained many elements that would define glam in the early 70s. "incluso hay sitios donde se refieren a él como el verdadero predecesor del glam porque realmente nos podemos remontar incluso a 1969 al primer trabajo que había hecho Joe Brieaz con su banda Pigeon en el cual he ya tenido un comportamiento verdaderamente glam."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: Life in California and Discovery by Jerry Brande (Post-1972)
podcast.body: After his difficult experience with the band Pigeon and his time in a psychiatric hospital, Joe Brieaz lived in poverty in California, residing in a completely abandoned and ruined apartment. During this period, he also resorted to prostitution to survive. It was under these circumstances that he was discovered by Jerry Brande, a significant talent scout of the 1970s. "vivía o mal vivía como podía en California de hecho vivía con un piso completamente abandonado y en ruinas al que se tenía también que dedicar a la prostitución y ahí es donde lo descubrió Jerry Brande."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: $500,000 Deal with Electric Records
podcast.body: His manager, Jerry Brandt, secured a deal with Electric Records for $500,000, which was an enormous sum of money at the time, underscoring the label's significant investment and belief in his potential. "That didn't stop a manager by the name of Jerry Brandt from striking a deal with the electric records for $500,000, a huge amount of money at the time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: AIDS Diagnosis and Death (1980s)
podcast.body: By the early 1980s, Gerbrieth's "bathhouse habits" led him to contract AIDS. He tragically died on August 3, 1987, notably just one week after his restrictive 10-year contract with Jerry Brandt expired. "By the early 80s, his bathhouse habits had caught up with him and Gerbrieth contracted AIDS."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Ambitious Stage Production for Paris Opera House
podcast.body: An additional $200,000 was allocated for a lavish stage production intended to open at the Paris Opera House. This production included elaborate props, such as a 40-foot model of the Empire State Building, which was designed to represent a phallic symbol. "Another $200,000 was spent on a stage production that was supposed to open at the Paris Opera House."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: Authentic Androgyne Identity
podcast.body: Joe Brieaz is considered perhaps the most authentic protagonist of the glam movement because his androgyne image was not merely a marketing component, unlike Marc Bolan or David Bowie. He had been a genuinely androgyne child, and this was his true personality from a very early age. "posiblemente Joe Brieaz fue el más auténtico de los protagonistas del movimiento glam porque no olvidemos que ni Marmola ni de Bid Bowie aunque tenían esa imagen andró general en verdad era mente homosexuales sino que era un muy importante componente de marketing pero Joe Brieaz era el verdadero andrógeno que había sido un niño andrógeno de ese niño y que realmente su personalidad era así y había sido así desde mucho antes."

podcast.title: Background as Part-time Drug Addict and Rent Boy
podcast.body: Before his major record deal, Gerbrieth had a background that included being a part-time drug addict and an occasional rent boy. This detail highlights the unconventional and challenging circumstances of his early life. "He was also a part-time drug addict and occasional rent boy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: Career Collapse and Contractual Issues
podcast.body: His career ultimately collapsed; the Paris shows never happened, and after two albums, Gerbrieth disappeared. He struggled to make music due to an "iron clad 10-year contract" with Jerry Brandt, with whom he was no longer communicating. "The Paris shows never happened and after two albums, Gerbrieth disappeared."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: Early Life and Child Prodigy Status
podcast.body: Joe Brieaz was an American artist who showed exceptional talent from childhood, being described as a true child prodigy. He is considered one of the great names lost to music history, with some referring to him as the true predecessor of glam. "Joe Brieaz es un artista americano que había sido un verdadero niño prodigio ya desde la infancia."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: Elektra Records Contract and Promotional Campaign
podcast.body: After being discovered by Jerry Brande, Joe Brieaz secured a major contract with Elektra Records for half a million dollars, representing a significant commercial opportunity for the United States to join the exploding global glam movement. Elektra Records invested heavily in his promotion, launching an extensive campaign through posters, magazines, and television. "él consigue gracias a Jerry Brande un primer contrato con el extra recorso por medio millón de dólares y la verdad es que para Estados Unidos era una gran oportunidad porque con el movimiento glam y con David Bowie explotando de popularidad en todo el mundo."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: Failed Tour Attempts
podcast.body: Due to his explicit homosexuality, eccentric behavior, and appearance, Joe Brieaz gained many enemies, hindering his career from the outset. He was unable to undertake a significant tour, as numerous venues directly refused to host his concerts. He had aspirations to tour Europe, specifically the Opéra Jaws de Paris, where glam music was highly demanded. "no llegó a casi poder hacer una gira porque hubo directamente un montón de sitios que se negaron a coger los conciertos de Joe Brieaz por su aspecto. Él quiso hacer una gira por Europa por justo además por la opera Jaws de Paris."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: First Openly and Genuinely Gay Rock Star
podcast.body: Gerbrieth (real name Bruce Campbell) is identified as the first rock singer to admit being 100% gay from the outset, making him the world's first openly and genuinely gay rock star. He was also the first gay singer to be signed to a major record label, Electric Records. "Gerbrieth, the world's first openly gay and genuinely gay rock star."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: Forced Retirement and Later Life
podcast.body: Following the commercial failure of his first and second albums with Elektra Records and the widespread societal rejection, Joe Brieaz was forced into retirement. He continued to live poorly, at one point staying in a luxury hotel but eventually returning to prostitution. He tragically died of AIDS in the 1980s, completely forgotten and buried from public memory. "Poco después él acababa haciendo su retirada pero bueno es una retirada prácticamente obligatoria ante el rechazo de la sociedad y él acabó un poco mal viviendo... acabaría moviendo de sidal primero en el 80."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: Forgotten Glam Figure
podcast.body: Jobriath is described as one of the great forgotten and hidden names of the Glam era. His re-edited album was previously almost impossible to find and highly sought after by Glam fans, indicating significant historical interest in his work. "Jobriaz, uno de los grandes nombres olvidados y escondidos de la época Glam."

podcast.title: Forgotten Glam Pioneer
podcast.body: Jobra is described as a fascinating but now almost forgotten figure from the birth of glam music, considered one of the "fathers of glam." "el casi olvidado Jobra, Jobra fue un personaje apasionante del nacimiento de la música glam que hoy ha quedado casi olvidado."

podcast.title: Gerbrieth AD Documentary
podcast.body: A documentary titled "Gerbrieth AD" provides further insight into his life and career, serving as a recommended resource for those interested in learning more about him. "there's a great documentary called Gerbrieth AD. How do you recommend it?"

podcast.title: Legacy as a Forgotten Genius and Documentary Controversy
podcast.body: Joe Brieaz's records were uncatalogued, forgotten, and unlisted until later influential artists, such as Morrissey, began referencing him as an important, forgotten genius. A documentary made a few years prior regarding Joe Brieaz is noted for its controversial portrayal, presenting him as a somewhat caricatured "great loser" who lacked talent, attempted to achieve success in David Bowie's shadow, and ultimately failed, which is criticized as a simplistic and exaggerated view of a complex figure. "es catalogados, olvidados hasta que grandes artistas postiliores pues como Morris y yo como muchos otros han tenido referencias a llobrias como lo importante que fue como ese genio olvidado. Tristemente tenemos también un documental que se hizo sobre llobria hace unos pocos años que también es bastante triste y que la verdad es que tiene también cierta controversia porque presentaré imagen de llobria un tanto de caricatura, un poco de gran perdedor que no tenía talento y que intentó destacar un poco a la sombra de David Bowie que no lo consiguió y que un poco era como un personaje ciertamente patético."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: Military Service and Psychiatric Confinement
podcast.body: After his first album with Pigeon failed in 1969, Joe Brieaz faced severe personal difficulties. He was called for military service, encountered numerous problems, escaped, was eventually caught by military police, arrested, and subsequently confined to a psychiatric hospital for a prolonged period due to his homosexuality. "lo llamaron para el servicio militar del tubo un montón de problemas acabó escapándose lo acabaron cogiendo la policía meditario lo acabó arrestando acabó encerrado en un psiquiátrico durante un montón de tiempo por ser homosexual."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: Pioneer of Glam Ahead of David Bowie
podcast.body: His recordings from late 1968 and 1969 suggest that David Bowie's work in the early 70s might not have been as innovative as commonly believed. Joe Brieaz, along with Marc Bolan, was developing glam two or three years before Bowie, indicating that Bowie might not have been the "great inventor" of glam, though he did lead it to its "golden age." "uno se da cuenta de que a lo mejor lo que hacía de David Bowie a primeros de los 70 no era tan tan innovador y que de David Bowie posiblemente no fue el gran inventor de la música clãm porque ya no es o llobria, teníamos también a Marvolan dos, tres años antes que él."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: Posthumous Rediscovery by Morrissey
podcast.body: Joe Brieaz's work remained largely forgotten until Morrissey, during his solo tour, discovered Brieaz's figure and was completely captivated by his material. Morrissey attempted to organize fundraising and provide artistic support, unaware that Joe Brieaz had been dead for many years. "Morris y durante la gina de solitario de llora Arsenal que descubría la figura de llobria así que ha completamente innotizado por su material y quiso hacer un poco de intentar ayudar a recodar fondos y de ayudarlo como artista sin darse de cuenta de que llobria llevaba ya muchos años muerto."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: Self-Reference as "True Fairy"
podcast.body: In interviews, Gerbrieth candidly referred to himself using the term "true fairy," openly embracing his identity at a time when such declarations were unprecedented in mainstream rock. "And in interviews, Gerbrieth referred to himself as a true fairy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Early Days of LGBTQ Rock

podcast.title: Societal Resistance and Perceived Lack of Talent
podcast.body: Joe Brieaz's career faced immense challenges, primarily due to the conservative American society that viewed the glam movement with suspicion, particularly when it came from American artists with such an appearance. Additionally, he was perceived to lack the exceptional talent of David Bowie or the guitar prowess of Marc Bolan, sometimes reducing him to a "caricature." "Por un lado teníamos una sociedad muy conservadora todavía en Estados Unidos que miraba con recelo todo este movimiento glam que venía del otro lado del charco... Joe Brieaz posiblemente no tenía ese gran talento que tenía David Bowie o esa increíble habilidad para tocar la guitarra que tenía Marmolan y se quedó un poco en un personaje a veces un tanto de caricatura."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: Television Performances
podcast.body: Despite the struggles with touring and societal acceptance, Joe Brieaz did manage to perform on television. Two of these performances are described as "authentic artistic jewels," providing a glimpse into his work from before the main glam era of the early 70s. "Lo que sí llegó es actuar en televisión, tenemos dos actuaciones de la televisión que son dos auténticas joyas de arte."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: Whitewashed from Rock History and Posthumous Recognition
podcast.body: For a long time, Gerbrieth's existence was "basically whitewashed from rock history." It is only recently, thanks to a dedicated group of fans (including Morrissey) who discovered him after his death, that he is beginning to receive acknowledgment for his significant contributions to music. "for a long, long time, his existence was basically whitewashed from rock history."
